messages:
sam: Heads-up — we need to change routing behavior for some VPC/on‑prem tenants. After the autoscaler flip we saw fallback attempts to hosted variants that their egress blocks, causing a bunch of 502/timeout noise. Can we propose a safe behavior?

yesha: Reproduced on staging with tenant T123 (egress deny to 0.0.0.0/0). Our runtime tried to route to hosted 'rwd-hosted-v2' in us-east1 and got tripped at the network layer. The control plane had no pre-check for tenant egress capability.

vincent: Quick options: 1) runtime agent implements local-only fallback (prefer local variants); 2) control plane makes the decision up-front and returns a `fallback_allowed=false`; 3) queue a provisioning flow to spin up a private worker and retry. I prefer (1) for lowest latency but it needs policy awareness.

nina: UX: console should expose per-tenant 'fallback mode' — choices: `Allow remote`, `Local only`, `Fail fast`. Also need telemetry in dashboards to surface when remote fallback was attempted but blocked.

sam: Implementation debate: do we put policy logic in the control plane (answers questions like \"is hosted fallback allowed for this tenant/region?\") or keep it entirely in the runtime agent which will just observe network errors? Control-plane pre-check avoids wasted attempts.

yesha: If runtime agent picks local variants, we also need a quality/degradation plan. Some customers expect parity; others accept reduced quality. Need per-tenant quotas or token-weighted accounting when we serve a smaller variant.

vincent: Proposed policy shape (example):
```json
{"tenant_id":"T123","allowed_regions":["eu-west1"],"fallback_policy":"local_then_fail","fallback_variants":["small-q4","tiny-int8"],"reject_remote":true}
```
This would let the router know to avoid any remote-hosted endpoints and try the listed local variants first.

nina: Console fields: `Fallback mode`, `Allowed regions`, `Fallback variants`, `Reject remote fallback`. Metrics: `fallback_rate`, `fallback_success_rate`, `remote_blocked_events`, `avg_latency_delta`, `token_cost_delta`. Add an explicit alert when `remote_blocked_events > 0.5%` of requests for a tenant.

sam: Telemetry: add routing.decision tags: `routing.decision.{allow_remote,deny_remote,local_fallback,fail_fast}` with tenant/model/region. Also log `routing.attempt.remote.host` for traces so we can correlate firewall denies.

devops-bot: :rotating_light: incident noted: routing.errors > 5% for tenant T123 — created ticket INC-789 and assigned to eng-platform.

yesha: Test plan: create a synthetic tenant with egress deny and verify three things — (A) control-plane pre-check (if present) returns `fallback_allowed=false` with reason `egress_restrictions`; (B) runtime respects that flag and does local fallback variants or returns `409 fallback_not_allowed`; (C) console surfaces the `remote_blocked_events`.

vincent: Implementation plan I will PR: (a) extend control-plane policy store to include `reject_remote` + allowed_regions; (b) add `/route` response field: `{fallback_allowed: bool, fallback_reasons: [string], fallback_variants: [string]}`; (c) runtime uses that to decide — if `fallback_allowed` is false and there are local variants, try them; else fail-fast. Will add unit tests to simulate egress deny responses.

nina: :thumbsup: Also add a migration: existing public tenants default to `reject_remote=false`, Private/VPC tenants default to `reject_remote=true` unless they opt-in. UX doc + console toggle required.

sam: OK. Sync tomorrow 10:00 to lock API schema and telemetry keys. @vincent please draft the API schema + a short migration plan before the meeting.

vincent: Will do — aiming for a PR by EOD with schema, sample policy JSON, and a migration script that tags existing tenants.
